$comment: Topics, `topic slug -> { doorway, cluster, ccc, lead, csdc, canons, documents }`, merged into
the shipped index by scripts/sync-corpus.mjs and read by /quaestiones and /quaestiones/{slug}.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS RATHER THAN A FIELD IN the corpus's build/*/manifest.json: the reason
descriptions.json and document-tags.json each give. Those manifests are GENERATED, a re-parse
rewrites them, and this project fixes parsers by re-parsing. A topic is editorial -- it is
somebody's judgement that a reader's question is answered HERE -- so it lives in tracked
source and is merged in on the way to the site.
WHAT A TOPIC IS NOT: it is not a subject. `site/document-tags.json` holds the subjects, and
they are browse axes over documents -- `labour`, `ecclesiology` -- chosen so a facet row
partitions the document set. Nobody arrives at a facet. They arrive at `my father died`, or
`I cannot stop`, or `is my first marriage still binding`, and docs/research/topics.md is the
pass that worked out the difference. The four DOORWAYS below are that finding: the argument
(tribal, public, googled mid-fight), the life event (something happened on Tuesday), the
private shame (2 a.m., and they would never ask a person) and the ordinary question.
A CLUSTER IS A SHELF INSIDE A DOORWAY and exists because a doorway is not a heading a
reader can scan. `argument` holds sixty topics; under one heading that is a wall, and the
reader who came asking whether any of it is true has to read past contraception and the
death penalty to find out. So `clusters` declares an ORDERED list per doorway, each topic
names one, and the landing page draws the SIXTEEN SHELVES and nothing above them. The
order inside a cluster is this file's, which is a judgement like `lead` is: within
`the-rules` love comes first, being the sentence the other thirteen are met with, and
contraception second, being the teaching the most readers doubt.
THE DOORWAY NO LONGER APPEARS ON THE PAGE, and it is still the axis of this file. It says
WHY a topic is where it is and it sets the order the shelves are drawn in; what it cannot
do is head a section, because `what people argue about` is true of all sixteen shelves and
the widest doorway held sixty topics across six of them. The level that tells a reader
where to go was always the one underneath. Keep filing by doorway; it is the question this
file is edited by, and dropping it would leave the clusters an unordered flat list.
CLUSTERS ARE NOT LATIN and slugs are, which is not an inconsistency. A slug is an ADDRESS
-- it appears in the URL and has to name the same thing in every language. A cluster is a
heading, appears in no address, and is a key into the dictionaries exactly as `doorway` was.
A CLUSTER HEADING NAMES ITS CONTENTS, which is a change from how they were first written.
They were situations -- `Whether any of it is true`, `Why am I not allowed to` -- matching
the doorways above them. With the doorways gone these sixteen are the whole navigation of
the page, read cold and shut, so each has one line to say what is behind it. The QUESTIONS
are still written as somebody's own words; the shelf they sit on is not.
THE SAME SUBJECT IS OFTEN TWO TOPICS, and the pairs below are deliberate rather than
duplicated. `abortus` is the argument and `post-abortum` is the woman who has had one;
`fecundatio-artificialis` is the case against IVF and `sterilitas` is the couple who cannot
conceive, leading on CCC 2379 rather than on the prohibition; `homosexualitas` is the
teaching and `homosexualitas-vivenda` is the person living under it; `mors-voluntaria` is a
bereavement and `mortis-desiderium` is the reader themselves; `adulterium` is the person who
did it and `infidelitas-coniugis` is the one it was done to. Where the two doors produce the
SAME anchor set and the same order, there is one topic and not two.
THE ANCHOR IS A CATECHISM SPAN, AND THE PASSAGES ARE NOT CHOSEN HERE. That is the whole
posture of the file. CCC 2357 already carries `Gen 19:1-29; Rom 1:24-27; 1 Cor 6:10;
1 Tim 1:10` and `CDF, Persona humana 8` in its own footnotes, and ProseBlocks linkifies them
wherever that paragraph is rendered -- so naming the span gets the Scripture and the
magisterial citation for free, chosen by the Catechism rather than by us. Where the span is
one of the Catechism's OWN headings (`Chastity and homosexuality` is `[2357, 2359]` in
build/ccc.en/structure.json) the editorial act is smaller still: the topic IS the heading.
THREE WORKS ARE QUOTED AND ONE IS LISTED, which is the distinction the fields draw. `ccc`,
`csdc` and `canons` name spans of works this site renders a numbered unit at a time, and the
topic page prints their text in that order; `documents` names whole works, which cannot be
quoted at a topic's length, so it prints their titles and leads to them.
`csdc` IS FOR THE QUESTION THE CATECHISM ANSWERS IN A PARAGRAPH AND THE COMPENDIUM IN A
CHAPTER. The Catechism's treatment of the social questions is real and short -- work is CCC
2426-2433, private property 2402-2407, the political community 2234-2246 -- because it is a
catechism and those are its summaries. The Compendium of the Social Doctrine is the developed
teaching those summaries stand on, addressed the same way, at `/doctrina-socialis/{n}`. So a
topic in the public square carries both: the Catechism says the thing, the Compendium works
it out. It is named where the Compendium ADDS, and 99 of the 128 topics have no `csdc`
because it does not: there is nothing there about purgatory or scruples.
`canons` USED TO BE A LIST OF NUMBERS and now prints the canon. That is why can. 1176 is on
`crematio` and can. 983 on `confessio-sacerdoti`: a reader asking whether the Church allows
cremation, or whether a priest may repeat what he heard, is answered by the law's own
sentence and was not answered by a link reading `1176`. A canon is named where the Code
holds the answer and the Catechism only names it -- a procedure, a permission, a condition.
THE SPAN IS STILL SHORT IN ALL THREE. A topic is read at one sitting by somebody who came
with a question, and the Compendium's chapters run to a hundred sections: `labor` names six
of them and not the chapter. The rest of it is one link away, at the paragraph the span
opens on.
EVERY `documents` ENTRY IS CHECKED AGAINST site/descriptions.json, which is the one place
here that says what a document is ABOUT rather than what it is called. A title is a poor
oracle and a Latin incipit is a worse one: `veritatis-splendor` sounds like the document
for faith and works and is about the moral act, so it was named under `iustificatio` until
its description was read; `signum-magnum` sounds like the document for apparitions and is
an exhortation on Marian devotion. Both were wrong and neither was findable by title.
Read the description before naming a document, and again before removing one.
`lead` IS THE ONE REAL JUDGEMENT IN THIS FILE, and it is one field wide so it can be argued
with. A span renders in paragraph order unless `lead` names a paragraph to put first. It
reorders the CATECHISM and only the Catechism, because that block opens the page and is the
one a reader meets before deciding whether to go on; the Compendium and the Code are read
further down, by somebody who has already decided to. It is
needed because the Catechism's order is systematic and a reader in trouble is not: CCC
2280-2283 opens on the gravity of suicide and closes on `We should not despair of the eternal
salvation of persons who have taken their own lives`, and a bereaved mother served those four
paragraphs in printed order meets three she cannot bear before the one she came for. Same for
2357 before 2358, and for the reader who has already had the abortion.
This is closer to editorialising than anything else on the site does, and it was taken
deliberately (2026-09-09, by direction) on the ground that the alternative is not neutrality:
printed order is itself an ordering, chosen by someone else for a reader who is not this one.
NOTHING IS OMITTED BY IT -- `lead` reorders a span and never trims one, so the paragraph a
reader is spared first is still on the page.
`brief` IS A TL;DR THE CATECHISM WROTE ITSELF. Every article of the Catechism ends with a
run of summary paragraphs printed under its own heading -- IN BRIEF, EN BREF, Resumindo,
KURZTEXTE -- and the corpus already carries the flag: `in_brief` on 548 of the 2,865
paragraphs, in all nine editions, because the Church wrote the summary in nine languages
and this site did not have to. So a topic may name a few of them to print above its own
passages, and the page gains a short answer without gaining a sentence of ours. That is the
whole reason the field is numbers and not prose: `docs/decisions.md` §Posture forbids a
gloss confusable with its source, and a summary somebody here composed out of sixteen
paragraphs would be exactly that -- our voice, in the Catechism's place, at the top of the
page, where a reader in a hurry would read it INSTEAD of the quotation and carry it away as
the Church's. A number cannot do that. It resolves to text with an address behind it, and
the reader can click 509 and land on the paragraph.
THE EDITORIAL ACT IS THE SELECTION AND IS THE SAME SIZE AS `lead`'s. An article's IN BRIEF
summarises the ARTICLE, not the question -- 2680-2682 close the article on prayer to the
Father, the Son and the Spirit, and only the last of the three is about Mary. So the field
is a list and not a span, the order is the answer's and not the Catechism's, and the page
says both. The checks that keep it honest are in sync-corpus.mjs: every number must be a
paragraph the Catechism itself flagged `in_brief`, so this cannot quietly become a field
for quoting whatever paragraph reads best; and no number may also be inside the topic's own
`ccc` spans, since a paragraph printed in the summary and again in the body is read twice
and the summary stops being one.
IT IS NOT WANTED ON EVERY TOPIC. A topic anchoring four paragraphs is already read at one
sitting, and a brief over it is a heading over a repetition -- the same argument `csdc` is
held to. Name it where the passages run long and the reader arrived at a WALL: `beata-virgo`
is sixteen paragraphs answering somebody who asked why Catholics give her so much, and the
five named there say Mother of God, immaculate, ever-virgin, assumed, and prayed WITH -- in
five sentences the Church already treats as the short form of those sixteen.
A SPAN LIST IS IN READING ORDER AND IS NOT SORTED, which is the cheaper half of the same
judgement and needs no field. `post-contraceptionem` opens on CCC 1735, on imputability, and
reaches 2370 after it; `scrupulositas` opens on the acts of the penitent and closes on 1735.
Nothing downstream re-sorts, so a span moved here moves on the page.
SLUGS ARE LATIN, like every other address here, and where the Catechism has its own word for
the thing the slug takes it -- `divinatio` is CCC 2116's, checkable against ccc.la. An address
names the same topic in every language and takes no interface prefix, which is the
distinction site/docs/addresses.md rests on; an English slug would quietly make English the
language the site is addressed in.
THE WORD `quaestio` NOW MEANS TWO THINGS ON THIS SITE and that is known, not overlooked
(2026-09-09, by direction). `/doctores/summa/{part}` addresses the Summa's quaestiones, which
are a unit of a text somebody else wrote; these are a reader's questions, which are ours. The
copy on both pages names its own sense rather than relying on the word.
THE VOCABULARY OF DOORWAYS AND CLUSTERS IS CLOSED, and sync-corpus.mjs exits 1 on a topic
outside it, on a cluster this topic's own doorway does not declare, on a
CCC span naming a paragraph this build has not got, on a document slug naming no document, on
a canon or a Compendium section this build has not got, and on a `lead` outside its own
topic's CCC spans. The last is the
one worth stating: a `lead` that has drifted out of its span is invisible on the page, because
a page that silently renders in printed order looks exactly like a page nobody wrote a `lead`
for.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT is recorded in docs/research/topics.md: a topic the corpus cannot
answer properly does not ship. Addiction has CCC 2290-2291 and nothing else; grief that does
not lift has the Catechism on the meaning of death and nothing addressed to the one left
behind; yoga waits on `Orationis Formas`; the Latin Mass on `Traditionis Custodes`;
same-sex blessings on `Fiducia Supplicans`, which is the worst of them, since the three
earlier documents ARE here and a stale answer reads exactly like a current one. Adding a
topic is a deliberate act -- it is a claim that a reader asking this will be better served
than not asking.
THE TITLES AND THE QUESTIONS ARE NOT HERE. They are prose a reader reads, so they are
`quaestiones.{slug}.*` in the i18n dictionaries like every other word of chrome, and until all
thirty-seven carry them this route stays out of CHROME_PATHS on route-manifest.ts's own terms.
